analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one paragraph (head ~670-690) describing a new dense-Qwen scheduling behavior. When the paged complete store is used, EngineV2Factory.demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens sets CBv2SchedulerConfig.demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens. A range then ends at the deepest aligned boundary at least 64 tokens below the prompt end, and only when that saves at least the store floor. The base text covers this region only by the surrounding context (base 667-670); the added text exists only in the patch excerpt, so the implementation is not visible here.

Security relevance is the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041, A-001, TB-007). The documented change affects checkpoint capture geometry for dense Qwen. The doc says the following are unchanged: the store write gate, the 'request the store would write' condition, fleet-novel refusal, first/target/latest retention, the three-boundary cap, and byte admission. That suggests no new at-rest artifact kinds, no new identity fields, and no TTL or HMAC changes. Capture may be more frequent at deeper boundaries, so write volume and the timing-oracle surface (SEC-035, same-account) could shift slightly. That is within the accepted-risk class. Those writes remain bound by the existing endurance and disk guards, 30-minute TTL, HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt scoping and AES-GCM.

No doc text loosens the TTL, the authenticated scope, the per-donation gating or the key derivation. Open questions for code-level review, not findable from this doc diff: whether the actual implementation in EngineV2Factory and DemandedShortCheckpointRange.swift honors the unchanged fleet-novel and write-gate checks. Also whether the cut introduces a restore-correctness or isolation issue beyond the claimed token-exact dense-Qwen parity. These cannot be judged from the documentation alone. No finding is warranted.
